name: level1-playthrough-revolt
description: Level 1 worker revolt scenario: aggressive krackle blasts, no well-being buildings, long tick cycles with events to trigger worker rebellion

steps.description: #553: staffed:true hires and equips, for free, employee #1 driller (blasting lvl1, driving.drill_rig lvl1) through #5 driver, plus vehicles #1 drill_rig through #4 rock_fragmenter (all unmanned). Cost is free -- does not change starting cash. The file's own 7 hand-hired employees below become #6-#12.

#553: staffed:true does NOT auto-assign a driver -- the free drill_rig (vehicle #1) is still a mesh nobody can drive until employee #1, the only qualified driller on the roster at this point, boards it. #921: Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls removed; vehicles are now claimed automatically by a qualified employee when a vehicle-gated task needs one, so this step runs as a direct bootstrap primitive instead of a click.

#553 sandbox-measured finding: staffed:true parks its 4 vehicles in a row at (0,2)/(2,2)/(4,2)/(6,2), and on dusty_hollow's terrain that row sits inside the map's only ramp corridor out of the spawn corner -- tickVehicleOnNavGrid recomputes the same A* path every tick (avoidVehicles:false) and only refuses the immediate next cell if another vehicle already occupies it (isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle), so the drill_rig (vehicle #1) advances exactly one cell to (1,2) and then waits forever behind the unmanned debris_hauler parked at (2,2) -- confirmed by direct trace: 40+ ticks stuck at (1,2), waitingTicks climbing, holeCount never leaving 0. This file never uses a debris_hauler, rock_digger or rock_fragmenter (zero hauling/fragment-breaking anywhere in its script), so scrapping the blocker -- and the other two idle vehicles that would otherwise just draw maintenance upkeep for nothing -- clears the corridor and turns dead weight into cash.
rock_digger #3 was never in the drill_rig's path, but this file has no use for it either -- scrapped for the same reason as #2: pure upkeep with nothing to show for it.

rock_fragmenter #4, same reasoning. Sandbox-measured residual proceeds across all three scraps ($10,000 + $20,000 + $12,800 = $42,800) fund the 7 hires below without touching the $50,000 opening balance.
#553: this and the following 6 hires are the file's own original crew, renumbered #6-#12 now that staffed:true claims #1-#5 first.

#553: employee #7. Deliberately left unlicensed for driving.drill_rig -- sandbox-measured, licensing this driller as a backup only adds a second casualty to blast 1 (they end up standing near the pattern too) without changing the outcome, since patterns 2-4 stall on the missing vehicle regardless of how many licensed drillers are left alive (see the note on the pattern-2 drill_plan step below).

expect.note: #596/#597-followup: this 168-tick request completes in full (sandbox-measured: 175->343, all 168 ticks) -- tickCount converted equals->changedBy (issue #596) since the batch running to completion, not a specific running total, is this step's own point. safety drops to a plain 50 (was 56.6): the earlier event is now union_unlucky_days, which carries no safety delta, so there is no tremor bump left to decay from. Along the way, 12 employees' payroll with zero income anywhere in this file crosses the $5,000 threshold and BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100 (Bankruptcy.ts) completes at tick 209 -- bankruptcy fires mid-drill, well before this pattern finishes, let alone blasts. Ticking does not stop when levelEnded flips (tickCommand only refuses to advance on a *pending event*, confirmed by direct trace), so the drill run itself completes normally on top of an already-lost game. wellBeing also crashes to 0 during this stretch (fatigue collapse with no living quarters anywhere in this file) and never recovers for the rest of the run except one brief bump (see the pattern-2 gap below).

Every panel control here sits at z-panel (100, tokens.ts), so the overlay covers charge-all just like it does in level2-playthrough-win.json and level3-playthrough-win.json's identical finding -- same overlay class, this file's own bankruptcy trigger instead of theirs. `expect.blocked` proves the real block; the underlying command still runs directly (bypassing the UI a player no longer has), so this pattern's 16 holes really do charge and the rest of this file's own trajectory (5 deaths at blast 1, destroyed rig, eventual revolt) keeps holding exactly as before -- only the UI-reachability half of the old assertion was wrong.

steps.description: #554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing. #554-followup (this session): the speed button itself is unreachable by this point -- bankruptcy fired at tick 209, inside the tick-168 step two checkpoints back, and every later charge/sequence/blast step's own notes already document the resulting full-viewport bankruptcy overlay (z-index 9999) covering every panel control for the rest of the run. `awaitUsable` followed by `clickSelector` against the speed button still hits that same overlay -- `awaitUsable`'s probe resolves (the button itself is neither disabled nor hidden), but the click that follows lands on the overlay in front of it (`element is covered by div`), sandbox-reproduced. Unlike the ~53 other files this speed-up fix was ported to, none of which have already gone bankrupt by their own equivalent step, this file's own premise is bankruptcy landing mid-drill, before pattern 1 even finishes -- so the overlay is already up here specifically. Uses `time speed:8` via the `time` console command instead -- explicitly carved out of the setup role's allowlist as a player affordance separate from state-mutating commands (`TIME_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST`, `scripts/shared/interaction-types.ts`) precisely because it models the same speed button without going through the DOM, so it lands the same time-scale change without depending on a control the overlay has already permanently covered. Resets back to `time speed:1` immediately once the wait resolves, as a minimal-footprint discipline (this fix should only touch the one step it exists for) -- sandbox-tested, and it does NOT by itself resync the rest of the file: the divergence documented on the next guard step's own note (a real event, not the file's long-pinned politics_competitor_mine, showing up here in interaction mode) persists identically whether speed is reset afterward or left at 8x, so it is set here during the wait itself (real ticks genuinely need to run faster than 1x to drain a 16-hole charge queue within timeoutMs's 120s budget, sandbox-confirmed necessary), not by anything that happens once the wait is already done. The reset is kept anyway, since leaving speed elevated for the rest of a 500+-tick file with no further reason to run fast has no upside and this session found none.

steps.description: #554-followup (this session, issue #586 CI): in COMMAND mode this event is still politics_competitor_mine (Price War, no wellBeing effect) -- confirmed by a full, clean command-mode run of this exact file with every #596/#597-era value below unchanged. In INTERACTION mode this checkpoint genuinely draws a different event: sandbox-reproduced identically across three independent runs as Neighbor Collapse (options: Send Rescue / Poach Contracts / Safety Audit Response) at tick 471, whose option 0 ("Send Rescue") lands a real wellBeing bump alongside its cash decrease. This is not an effect of leaving speed elevated after step 27's wait (disproved: resetting to `time speed:1` immediately after that wait changes nothing about which event draws here) -- draining a 16-hole charge queue in real time at all, regardless of speed, is enough real-clock-driven tick accrual to cross this event's own eligibility threshold, the same real-time-accrual-drift class this file's other notes already document for cash/ecology/nuisance, just large enough here to change which event fires rather than nudge a number. Issue #586 CI's own report ("wellBeing should be 0 but is 4") is this exact checkpoint, diverging by a different magnitude yet again (CI: 4, this sandbox: 8) -- two independently-observed non-zero readings at the same checkpoint, neither matching command mode's 0, confirms this is a genuine command/interaction split, not one fixed wrong number to re-pin. wellBeing is otherwise this scenario's own subject and stays `equals` everywhere else in this file (crashes to 0 and never recovers) -- this one checkpoint is the sole exception, and is dropped from `equals` rather than pinned to any single one of the (at least) three different real values now on record for it, the same treatment this file already gives cash/ecology/nuisance once they're confirmed to vary this way. `decreased: [cash]` still holds in every environment observed (command and both interaction runs), so it stays. tickCount dropped from this step's own expect for the same reason as the tick-283/event-choose-0 step earlier in this file -- it doesn't move during an event-choose, and the tick-10 step above already covers it directionally. Interaction-mode finding (issue #586 CI): unlike the file's other post-bankruptcy events, this one is genuinely unreachable, not a covered-by-div race -- sandbox-reproduced (scripts/_repro_temp.ts-class harness replay, real Puppeteer clicks throughout): the tick-10 step above's own blast (0-hole ghost, same as the pattern-2/3/4 blasts throughout this file) arms BlastReportModal's 3-real-second open delay (BLAST_REPORT_DELAY_MS, BlastReportModal.ts); UIManager.update (UIManager.ts:421) defers EventModal.update entirely while that report is pending-or-visible, so the event dialog never opens and #bs-event-dialog still holds stale, hidden .bs-event-choice nodes from the PREVIOUS (already-dismissed) event -- exactly the kind of stale-node trap a bare waitForSelector(selector) can't tell apart from a live dialog, which is what produced Puppeteer's own "Node is either not clickable or not an Element" against a display:none ancestor. Confirmed via __probeSelector that this is not a race that a longer wait fixes: right now the blast report's own Close button reads "hidden" (still inside its 3s delay); left running past that delay it flips to "covered" -- LevelEndScreen's z-index 9999 sits above BlastReportModal's shared z-index 600 (unlike the event dialog's own 10500, styles.ts), so once armed, the report can never be dismissed post-bankruptcy either, and the event stays gated behind it permanently. `blocked` proves the report's Close button (the real control standing between the player and this event) while `event choose 0` still runs directly, in whichever mode is running, to keep the rest of the file's trajectory intact.

expect.note: #553-followup (issue #586 CI): the report-close button this proves against is present but hidden the instant the event fires (still inside BlastReportModal's 3s real-time open delay) -- a stronger, later-timed probe against the same control reads 'covered' once the delay elapses, matching the bankruptcy overlay's own z-index over every z-index:600 modal elsewhere in this file. Either reading proves the same permanent block; 'hidden' is what a probe taken this early and reliably observes.
